parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminal offence, no documented border or facility exclusion, no police targeting, and no documented violence against trans visitors. Open public life (annual trans march, two-decade pride), a conversion-therapy ban, constitutional equality protection covering sexual orientation, and anti-discrimination statutes show a generally accepting society and functioning recourse. The surgery-gated ID regime is resident-facing: a visitor carries a home passport, so it is a climate signal, not an exposure. Friction keeps this below the top tier: restroom discrimination is documented among trans respondents, most government all-gender toilets fail standards (mitigated by an active national expansion program), the anti-gender movement is rising, and border treatment of trans visitors is unresolved in the record. No universal-exposure or state-tolerated targeting feature appears; worst documented features are service friction plus thin visitor-specific evidence.
